blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: Every Kubernetes file starts with two lines: the API version and the kind of object to create.
blocks.why: Kubernetes reads these lines first, so it knows which rules apply to the rest of the file.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Pod, from the core v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.what: The name is how you find the Pod later, for example with kubectl get pod web. Labels are tags.
blocks.why: Each Pod in a namespace needs its own name. Other objects find Pods by their labels.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without a name, Kubernetes rejects the Pod. Without labels, it still runs, but nothing can select it.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Pod, and a label to group it
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: web
  labels:
    app: web

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: The spec says what you want Kubernetes to run. Here it is one container started from the nginx image.
blocks.why: A Pod needs at least one container. The image is your packaged app, which Kubernetes downloads and starts.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without containers, Kubernetes rejects the Pod. Without an image, the container cannot start.
blocks.comment: The container to run and the image it starts from
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: web
  labels:
    app: web
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4

blocks.title: Which port?
blocks.what: This records that the container listens on port 80, where nginx serves its web page.
blocks.why: It tells people and tools which port the app uses. The list is mostly informational.
blocks.ifRemoved: nginx still listens on port 80, so the Pod works the same. Readers just lose the hint.
blocks.comment: The port the app listens on inside the container
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: web
  labels:
    app: web
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Pods are in the core v1 API.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Pod runs one or more containers together.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name and labels.
notes.metadata.name: The Pod's name. It must be unique among Pods in the same namespace.
notes.metadata.labels: Key and value tags. Other objects use them to find this Pod.
notes.metadata.labels.app: A label with the key app and the value web. The key app is a common choice.
notes.spec: The desired state: what you want Kubernetes to run.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.containers[].image: The image to run, with a version tag. A fixed tag runs the same version every time.
notes.spec.containers[].ports: Ports the container listens on. This list is mostly informational.
notes.spec.containers[].ports[].containerPort: The port number the app listens on inside the container.
